excerpts.text: Of the 70 delegates chosen as representatives to the [Constitutional Convention](https://www.britannica.com/event/Constitutional-Convention) of 1787, only 55 actually attended the proceedings in Philadelphia, and it is believed that there were never more than 46 of them in attendance at any one time.

**Constitutional Convention**, (1787), in U.S. history, convention that drew up the [Constitution of the United States](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Constitution-of-the-United-States-of-America). Stimulated by severe economic troubles, which produced radical political movements such as [Shays’s Rebellion](https://www.britannica.com/event/Shayss-Rebellion), and urged on by a demand for a stronger central government, the convention met in the Pennsylvania State House in [Philadelphia](https://www.britannica.com/place/Philadelphia) (May 25–September 17, 1787), ostensibly to [amend](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/amend) the Articles of [Confederation](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Articles-of-Confederation). All the states except [Rhode Island](https://www.britannica.com/place/Rhode-Island-state) responded to an invitation issued by the [Annapolis Convention](https://www.britannica.com/event/Annapolis-Convention) of 1786 to send delegates. Of the 74 deputies chosen by the state legislatures, only 55 took part in the proceedings; of these, 39 signed the [Constitution](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Constitution-of-the-United-States-of-America). The delegates included many of the leading figures of the period. Among them were [George Washington](https://www.britannica.com/biography/George-Washington), who was elected to preside, [James Madison](https://www.britannica.com/biography/James-Madison), [Benjamin Franklin](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Benjamin-Franklin), [James Wilson](https://www.britannica.com/biography/James-Wilson-United-States-statesman), [John Rutledge](https://www.britannica.com/biography/John-Rutledge), [Charles Pinckney](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Charles-Pinckney), [Oliver Ellsworth](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Oliver-Ellsworth), and [Gouverneur Morris](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Gouverneur-Morris).
